counterfactual.change: Set sensor_noise from 0.015244803979671965 to 0.0, keeping all other fields (dt, steps=43, plant, initial, force_limit, seed, pushes) identical. Without measurement noise the controller stabilizes and no pole_upright violation occurs, proving noise-induced mis-estimation is causal.

explanation: Shrunk scenario shows sensor_noise-driven destabilization. With dt~0.015s and sensor_noise~0.015, the state-feedback controller receives noisy measurements of theta/omega each step. Gains adapt to the plant but noise causes persistent control error (forces ~37-42 N, well below limit). Over 43 steps (~0.65s) the pole angle and angular rate diverge: theta grows from 0.017 rad at step 0 to 0.22 at step 38, 0.44 at step 40, 0.71 at step 42, then 0.86 rad at step 43 exceeding the 0.8 rad pole_upright limit, with omega reaching ~10 rad/s and cart velocity ~-8 m/s. Energy rises to ~37.5 (vs ~1.45 initial) fed by controller work ~36.1, showing positive feedback. Removing only sensor_noise eliminates the violation, confirming noise as cause.
vision_note: The pole tilts progressively farther to the right from step 40 to 42, then at step 43 the tip turns red as the lean becomes visibly larger and exceeds the upright limit. The blue cart stays near the center of the track between the red walls without leaving the track in these frames.
